problem: Existing VLN benchmarks (R2R, VLN-CE) assume idealized wheeled or point agents with teleport or pseudo-motion, ignoring robot embodiment, locomotion dynamics (falls, stuck, viewpoint shifts) and lighting. How well current VLN methods transfer to physically realistic, cross-embodiment settings is unknown.
motivation: Real robots (humanoid, quadruped, wheeled) have different camera heights, gaits and controllers, and operate under varying illumination. A platform integrating realistic robot dynamics, RL locomotion controllers and scalable data collection is needed to measure the sim-to-physical gap and to train cross-embodiment models.
key_idea: Build VLN-PE, an Isaac Sim (GRUTopia) physically realistic VLN platform with humanoid/quadruped/wheeled robots, RL controllers, extra scenes (GRScenes, 3DGS) and fall/stuck metrics, then systematically benchmark ego-centric VLN pipelines (classification, diffusion RDP, map-based VLMaps).
insight: Models trained in pseudo-motion VLN-CE drop sharply when physics is added (SR drops of 10-18% for Seq2Seq-Full, CMA-Full, NaVid). Consistent locomotion controller between data collection and evaluation matters (Tab. controller_effect), and co-training on all three robots plus VLN-CE gives the best results per robot (e.g. Humanoid val-unseen SR 26.87 vs 18.78 single-robot). RGB-only NaVid is fragile to low light and 3DGS rendering noise, while RGB-D CMA/RDP are stable, and small fine-tuned models on tiny new-scene data beat zero-shot 7B NaVid, showing MP3D-style benchmarks under-measure generalization.
method: VLN-PE platform: built on GRUTopia/Isaac Sim; RL-based locomotion controllers for Unitree H1/G1 humanoids, Aliengo quadruped and Jetbot wheeled robot; 90 MP3D scenes converted to USD with floor holes manually fixed, aligned to VLN-CE coordinates; adjustable disk/camera lighting.

New scenes and datasets: GRU-VLN10 (10 GRScenes synthetic homes, 441/111/1,287 train/val-seen/val-unseen episodes) and 3DGS-Lab-VLN (160 train, 640 eval) with instructions from a modular LLM pipeline (NavComposer + GPT-4 + human filtering); R2R filtered of stair episodes (8,679/658/1,347).
Physical metrics: Fall Rate (roll>15° or pitch>35° or low CoM height) and Stuck Rate (<0.2 m and 15° change for 50 steps) added to TL/NE/OS/SR/SPL.

RDP (Recurrent Diffusion Policy): ego-centric RGB-D, LongCLIP for RGB and text, ResNet50 depth, GRU history, two cross-attention modules, transformer DDPM decoder predicting T=8 relative (dx,dy,dyaw) waypoints (execute 4), plus a stop-progress MLP head (loss weight lambda=10).

Baselines evaluated: Seq2Seq, CMA (and CMA-CLIP with Long-CLIP text encoder), NaVid (7B, zero-shot), RDP, and improved VLMaps (VLFM-style frontier exploration, CLIP room classification, A* local planner with reorientation cost).
Controller modes: flash (teleport-like), move-by-speed (RL legged/diff-drive), move-along-path (A*+PID for VLMaps); cross-embodiment data collection across three robots.

setting.backbone: Seq2Seq/CMA (~36M, trained from scratch or fine-tuned from VLN-CE weights), RDP (LongCLIP + ResNet50 + GRU + diffusion transformer, trained from scratch), NaVid 7B (frozen, zero-shot), VLMaps (LSeg + LLM, training-free)
setting.training_data: VLN-PE R2R data collected with robot controllers (8,679 train episodes, stairs filtered); cross-embodiment data from humanoid, quadruped, wheeled; VLN-CE weights with 175K augmented samples for Full baselines; 441 GRU-VLN10 / 160 3DGS episodes for fine-tuning
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D pinhole camera (RGB-only for NaVid)
setting.action_space: discrete FORWARD/TURN/STOP via move-by-speed controller (Seq2Seq/CMA/NaVid); continuous relative waypoints (dx,dy,dyaw) for RDP; A* path following for VLMaps
setting.simulator: Isaac Sim (GRUTopia) with MP3D, GRScenes and 3DGS scenes
setting.privileged: none for models (VLMaps builds map online); real-world test uses Unitree Go2 with RealSense D455

numbers_note: Own benchmark VLN-PE, not a canonical benchmark; only key rows listed. Real-world test (14 episodes, Go2): CMA fine-tuned on VLN-PE OS 57.14 / SR 28.57 vs 14.29 / 7.14 without.
results: On VLN-PE humanoid R2R val-unseen, zero-shot VLN-CE models drop sharply, while NaVid is best zero-shot (SR 22.42) and CMA+ fine-tuned reaches SR 23.31 / SPL 19.66; RDP trained from scratch (SR 21.98) beats CMA and Seq2Seq from scratch. Cross-embodiment co-training gives the best per-robot results (Humanoid val-unseen SR 26.87), and RGB-only NaVid drops SR by about 11-12 points under low or camera light.
limitations: Only ego-centric single-camera methods evaluated; panoramic waypoint methods (ETPNav etc.) are not covered
Locomotion controllers cannot handle stairs (episodes filtered); RDP is a simple baseline and NaVid could not be retrained (zero-shot only); VLMaps evaluated on only 200 episodes
Real-world validation is tiny (14 episodes, one robot); new datasets are small
